### 1. What Was Established This Turn (Quantitative Closures)

We completed the grand epistemic consilience by quantitatively modeling the final unaddressed fusion confinement paradigm (**Sheared-Flow Z-Pinch**), the critical material and liquid immersion blanket constraints (**FLiBe Beryllium reserve depletion & Pb-17Li MHD pressure drops**), the thermodynamic limits of **Direct Energy Conversion**, and a **10,000-trial stochastic Monte Carlo CPM simulation**:

1. **Sheared-Flow Stabilized Z-Pinch (Zap Energy Archetype): The Electrode Erosion & Insulator Flashover Wall**
   - **Bennet Equilibrium & Edge Field:** At $n_e = 10^{23}\text{ m}^{-3}$ and $r_p = 5.0\text{ mm}$, sustaining $T = 10\text{ keV}$ requires Bennet current $I = 0.709\text{ MA}$. At nominal $1.5\text{ MA}$ operating current, the self-magnetic field at the pinch edge reaches **$B_\theta = 60.0\text{ Tesla}$**, yielding an Alfven velocity of **$v_A = 2,619\text{ km/s}$**.
   - **The Microsecond Transit Trap:** Shumlak shear stabilization mandates an axial velocity $v_z \ge 0.1 v_A = \mathbf{261.9\text{ km/s}}$. Through a $1.5\text{ m}$ column, the plasma axial transit time is just **$\tau_{transit} = 5.73\text{ }\mu\text{s}$**. The entire plasma column is flushed and discarded every $5.7\text{ microseconds}$, demanding continuous supersonic fuel acceleration that heavily taxes net plant power.
   - **Electrode Arc Erosion Catastrophe:** A $1.5\text{ MA}$, $50\text{ }\mu\text{s}$ discharge transfers $45\text{ C/pulse}$. At standard tungsten arc erosion rates ($25\text{ }\mu\text{g/C}$), each pulse vaporizes $1.125\text{ mg}$. At $10\text{ Hz}$ and $80\%$ capacity factor, the electrodes vaporize **$0.778\text{ kg/day}$** (**$284.0\text{ kg/year}$**) of solid tungsten directly into the chamber. Sputtered tungsten ($Z=74$) impurity concentrations above $0.01\%$ radiate more power ($P_{rad} \propto Z^3 n_e n_W$) than fusion produces, causing instant radiative quench.
   - **Insulator Radiation-Induced Conductivity (RIC):** Ceramic insulators at $1\text{ m}$ standoff from a $50\text{ MW}$ neutron source absorb $1.5 \times 10^4\text{ Gy/s}$. Radiation-induced conductivity jumps **8 orders of magnitude** (from $10^{-14}\text{ S/m}$ to **$1.59 \times 10^{-6}\text{ S/m}$**), causing dielectric surface flashover and electrical breakdown under $50-100\text{ kV}$ pulse holdoff.

2. **Liquid Immersion Blankets & Critical Materials: The Beryllium Scarcity & MHD Pressure Trap**
   - **FLiBe Beryllium Global Exhaustion:** FLiBe salt ($2\text{LiF}-\text{BeF}_2$) contains **$9.11\text{ wt}\%\text{ Beryllium}$**. A standard $200\text{ m}^3$ immersion blanket (ARC archetype) requires **$35.36\text{ tonnes of pure Beryllium}$** per reactor.
   - Total global annual mine output of Beryllium (USGS 2024–2026 data) is only **$280.0\text{ tonnes/year}$**. A **single reactor consumes $12.63\%$ of the entire world's annual production**. Even allocating $50\%$ of planetary Beryllium production to fusion caps fleet buildout at **$\le 3.96\text{ reactors/year}$**. Mining expansion is legally and medically restricted due to incurable Chronic Beryllium Disease (CBD, OSHA Class A carcinogen).
   - **Liquid Metal Pb-17Li MHD Pressure Drop:** In a $12.0\text{ T}$ field, Pb-17Li experiences a Hartmann number of **$Ha = 13,416$** and Stuart number of **$N = 5,745$**. Lorentz drag drives an MHD pressure gradient of **$2.016\text{ MPa/m}$** and a total duct pressure drop of **$12.10\text{ MPa}$ ($121.0\text{ bar}$)**, requiring **$17.28\text{ MWe}$** of parasitic pumping power and bursting thin Eurofer97 channels ($S_m \approx 110\text{ MPa}$ at $500^\circ\text{C}$).

   - In pulsed FRC / Z-pinch direct conversion cycles, circulating magnetic energy $E_{mag}$ in high-field coils is $\approx 3\times$ the fusion yield ($300\text{ MJ}$ vs $100\text{ MJ}$).
   - With realistic capacitor and solid-state switch round-trip efficiencies ($85\%$ injection, $85\%$ recovery), round-trip electromagnetic dissipation consumes **$97.94\text{ MJ}$ per shot**.
   - With Bremsstrahlung radiating $27\%$ of D-$^3\text{He}$ power away at $75\text{ keV}$, net plant engineering electrical gain is **$Q_{eng} = 0.878 < 1.0$**. The plant operates as a **net electricity consumer** unless core plasma gain exceeds **$Q_{plasma} \ge 1.79$**.
